When @Starlink helped rescuers save nine fishermen from a flooding boat in Alaska. The United States Coast Guard confirmed that all nine people aboard the Arctic Sea were rescued. Their fishing boat had run aground near St. George Island in Alaska’s remote Bering Sea and was taking on water. Winds around 93 km/h and three-metre waves made it too dangerous for a nearby fishing boat, North Sea, to rescue the crew directly. North Sea used Starlink to stay connected throughout the response. Its crew also provided updates to the Coast Guard. A Coast Guard helicopter lifted all nine fishermen to safety. Starlink helped keep communications working during an emergency where nine lives were at risk. This life-saving technology should be available in every part of the world. Media

Facts by #JoeHansenFacts Why are Starlink's space lasers such a big deal? Without lasers, a satellite has to send your data straight back down to a ground station it can see. No ground station in range, no internet. Starlink skips that step. 1. Each V2 Mini satellite carries 3 lasers that talk directly to other satellites. 2. More than 24,000 of these lasers are up there now, forming one mesh around the planet. 3. Each link runs at up to 200 Gbps. SpaceX says hardware next year moves that to 400. 4. Data can hop from satellite to satellite until it finds a ground station, even on the other side of an ocean. That's why it works on a cruise ship in the middle of the Pacific, and why it kept working in Spain and Portugal when the whole power grid went down in April 2025. Smarter laser routing also cut 30 to 40 ms of latency in Asia and Africa in 2025.

The sudden collapse of the value of CoT (even summarized CoT) in the agentic era changes working with AI. Effectively steering AIs and getting any sort of observability now requires you to ask for interim outputs & tests, and to use AI help to troubleshoot problems you find.

It used to be that you could look at the CoT from a request and get a sense of where the model was going, but with tons of agents calling other agents, and CoTs that run to thousands of pages for even simple agentic tasks, that is no longer possible.

It also requires you to trust the orchestrator model more than ever, since it is the only thing that can track all of the tasks. Which means you need to use AI to both find problems with AI and to troubleshoot problems you find.
